A LaMDA, which stands for “Language Model for Dialogue Applications,” is a family of conversational large language models developed by Google. Originally introduced as Meena in 2020, LaMDA was designed to engage in open-ended conversations, making it unique in the realm of conversational AI. It is built on the Transformer architecture, a neural network model that Google Research invented and open-sourced in 2017. This architecture allows the model to understand the relationship between words and predict subsequent words, enabling more natural and intuitive interactions.
